title: Inertia and weight of a pair bound through the field, full grip

key_results.statement: Half-gap $\sigma_iR_i=\frac{N_f}2[\varepsilon_0(g_i)-\varepsilon_0(-g_i)]=ng_i[1+O(\eta^2)]$, $c_i^2=\sigma_iR_i/\mu_i=\tau_i^2[1+O(N_f\eta^2)]$, the part $M_i^o$ of the mutual term odd in $g_i$ ($M_1^o=M_2^o=B[1+O(\eta)]$), and the bond average $\bar f(\rho)=\frac14[f(\rho-1)+2f(\rho)+f(\rho+1)]$.

Full grip, band regime $\max\tau_i\ll d$, with $d$ the distance of $\mathcal G$ from all other held levels of its parity class, joint flip included ($d_\times\simeq2n|g_1+g_2|-\frac32|B(0)|$, nonresonance (N×) $d_\times\gg\max\tau_i$): the band contract is (2.10)/(6.1) with error $O(\tau^4/d^3)$, and the gap of the double step of $b_i$ across the relative bond $\rho$ from $r=\rho\mp1$ is $\Delta_i(r;\rho)=2\sigma_iR_i+M_i^o(r)+M_i^o(\rho)+M_i^e(r)-M_i^e(\rho)$.
Local inertia of each body: $m_i(\rho)=\mu_i+\bar M_i^o(\rho)/c_i^2+O(|\mu_i|\eta\eta_j)=\mu_i+\bar B(\rho)/\tau_i^2\,[1+O(\eta)]$; (6.5) and (6.6) hold for the full grip.

In the class (band regime with the nonresonance condition (N×), binding regime $w\ll L$, tuned near-zero cases excluded), the selected level is bound at $r\approx0$ iff $\tau_1^2g_2+\tau_2^2g_1>0$ ($g_i=\sigma_i\gamma_iM_i$): lowest if both $g_i>0$, highest for opposite signs, never for both $g_i<0$; otherwise the extreme level sits at $r\approx L/2$.

$D_0=1/E_b''(0)-\mu_1-\mu_2=D^{\rm lat}[1+O(\tau^2/d^2)]+D^{\rm mark}[1+O(\eta,\tau^2/d^2)]$ plus the ring remainder, with $D^{\rm lat}=(\mu_1+\mu_2)(1-\beta_0)/\beta_0$ and $D^{\rm mark}=\beta_0^{-2}\sum_\rho b_0\sum_i\bar M_i^o/c_i^2=(\tau_1^{-2}+\tau_2^{-2})\beta_0^{-2}\sum_\rho b_0\bar B\,[1+O(\eta)]$; both parts carry $1/\beta_0$ and the estimate holds for small $\beta_0$; it is (6.8) with $s_c=+1$, $c_i=\tau_i$.
Cost of the bond: $\Delta E_0=\langle M\rangle_0+K_0[1+O(\eta)]$, $K_0=\frac14(\mu_1^{-1}+\mu_2^{-1})(1-\beta_0)$.

Item 3 (i): $D_0-\Delta E_0/\tau_i^2=(4\mu_1\mu_2K_0/\beta_0)[1-\beta_0/(4\mu_1\mu_2\tau_i^2)]+(\langle M\rangle_0/\beta_0)[\tau_j^{-2}+(1-\beta_0)\tau_i^{-2}]$ up to $O((\eta+w/L+\tau^2/d^2)|D^{\rm mark}|+(\tau^2/d^2)|D^{\rm lat}|)$; the lattice term exceeds $K_0/v^2$ by a factor $\ge d^2/\tau_j^2$; for $g_1g_2<0$ both terms are positive and equality fails except in the limit of (7.8); for $g_1,g_2>0$ equality holds only on a tuned surface.

Item 3 (ii), regime $\delta_m=|\mu_1+\mu_2|(1-\beta_0)/(|B(0)|(\tau_1^{-2}+\tau_2^{-2}))\ll1$ (which implies $1-\beta_0\ll\eta$): $D_0=(\tau_1^{-2}+\tau_2^{-2})\Delta E_0[1+O(\eta,\delta_m,\tau^2/d^2)]$, i.e. $2\Delta E_0/v^2$ for $\tau_1=\tau_2=v$, not $\Delta E_0/v^2$; it approaches $\Delta E_0/\tau_i^2$ only as $\tau_i/\tau_j\to0$.
Weight gradient of a single held body on the ring: $W_i'=\phi'[ng_i+2\kappa_sC_i^{(2)}]$ up to relative $O(\eta^2)$, $C_i^{(2)}=-ng_i^2\ell_0/t_f$, $\kappa_s=(L^2(1-2u)^2+2)/(L^2-1)$, $u=s/L$.

Bond part of the weight gradient of the selected level (its first-order shift by a source at distance $s\gg w$ from the pair's midpoint, kinetic contribution included): $W_b'=\phi'[2\kappa_sB(0)+\langle V\rangle_0-K_0]+O(\eta|B(0)\phi'|)+O(|F\phi'|w^2/L)$.

Exactly $\Gamma_{\rm pair}=(\mu_1\Gamma_1+\mu_2\Gamma_2+D_0\Gamma_b)/(\mu_1+\mu_2+D_0)$ with $\Gamma_b=W_b'/D_0$; $\Gamma_i=\tau_i^2\phi'[1-2\kappa_sg_i\ell_0/t_f+O(\eta^2,N_f\eta^2,\tau^2/d^2)]$; at leading order $\Gamma_{\rm pair}=\beta_0\bar\Gamma$, equal to $\Gamma_1=\Gamma_2$ (for $1-\beta_0\to0$) iff $\tau_1=\tau_2$.

Regime $\delta_m\ll1$, $\eta\ll\kappa_s$, $w/L\ll\kappa_s$: $\Gamma_b=2\kappa_s\phi'/(\tau_1^{-2}+\tau_2^{-2})[1+O(\eta/\kappa_s,w/(L\kappa_s),\delta_m,\tau^2/d^2,\delta_m\tau^2/(\kappa_sd^2))]$; for $\tau_1=\tau_2$ the binding cost is weighed in the same proportion as its inertia, at leading order, only as $u\to0$, and at finite $u$, where $1-\kappa_s$ exceeds the remainders, less by $\kappa_s<1$, and $\Gamma_{\rm pair}-\bar\Gamma=4(1-\kappa_s)g_1g_2\ell_0\tau^2\phi'/(t_f(g_1+g_2))$; for $\tau_1\neq\tau_2$, $\Gamma_b=\Gamma_i$ only at the tuned distance $\kappa_s=(1+\tau_i^2/\tau_j^2)/2$, which exists iff $\tau_i<\tau_j$, and $\Gamma_b=\Gamma_1=\Gamma_2$ only for $\tau_1=\tau_2$ and $u\to0$.

At fixed $n,\gamma_i,M_i,\tau_i$: mark quantities scale as $t_f^{-1}$, lattice quantities as $t_f^{-2/3}$ ($w\gg1$), $D^{\rm lat}/|D^{\rm mark}|\propto t_f^{1/3}$, while $D^{\rm mark}/\Delta E_0\to\tau_1^{-2}+\tau_2^{-2}$ and $\Gamma_b/\Gamma_i\to2\kappa_s/(1+\tau_i^2/\tau_j^2)$ do not depend on $t_f$.

open_issues: The code has N_f = 1, so S5 is reached only at δ_m = 0.09 (S1) and 0.13 (S2), with L = 256; the remainders have sizeable coefficients (W_b′ − (7.10) up to 3.4 η|B(0)φ′|, the band contract misses 5–10% of D_0); the leading form of (7.12) is reproduced to 4–12% in S1 inside the S6 hierarchy and to 28–44% in S2, and at u = 1/16 the deficit 1 − κ_s is not resolved.
The kinetic weight −K_0 φ′ accounts for the difference between the exact selected level and the held-field average to 4–14% (S2), 9–30% (S1) and 16–45% (R); the excess grows with u and η.

The fall itself (time evolution) is not simulated; Γ is taken from (5.14), (6.13); W_0 is the first-order shift of the selected level at P = 0 with the source at a fixed distance from the midpoint, and the b_0/m form of (6.13) differs from it at relative O(1 − β_0) in ⟨V⟩_0.
Descriptions that violate (N×) (g_1 + g_2 near 0, e.g. g_1 = −g_2) would need a band contract on the group together with the jointly flipped sector; they are outside the class.
The factor κ_s is a property of the ring (zero mode); other geometries (tori) are out of scope.
c_i² = τ_i²[1+O(N_f η²)] is an estimate of the overlap corrections of (5.3), not derived in detail.

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions of (7.3), (7.5), (7.7), (7.8) and of the fall factors
Limit g2 → 0: mark and bond terms vanish linearly, m1 → μ1, w → ∞, (7.9) reduces to (4.5)
Coincident held pair r = 0 weighs as one coupling g1+g2 (C1+C2+B(0) = C_G)
